summary: Khalifa University in Abu Dhabi gives merit-based graduate scholarships to international students admitted full-time to its Master's and PhD programmes. Applicants are placed in a tier (I to IV) during admission, and the tier decides how much tuition is waived and whether a stipend, accommodation and other support are given. PhD awards come in a Research Path, which carries a work commitment after graduation, and a Study Path, which does not. Places are limited and meeting the minimum criteria does not guarantee an award.
eligibility_notes:
The scholarship is for international students enrolled full-time in a graduate programme at Khalifa University. There is no separate scholarship application: eligibility is checked during the admission process, places are limited, and meeting the minimum criteria does not guarantee an award. Applicants are mapped to a tier using academic merit, research potential (for PhD) and other factors that fit university priorities. The tier is stated in the admission offer.

Master's admission: a bachelor's degree in a relevant discipline with a minimum CGPA of 3.0 out of 4.0 (or equivalent, for example upper second-class honours) from a reputable accredited institution.

Regular PhD (with a master's): a bachelor's in a relevant discipline with CGPA 3.0 out of 4.0, and a master's in a relevant discipline with CGPA 3.25 out of 4.0, or equivalent.

Direct PhD (no master's): a bachelor's in a relevant discipline with CGPA 3.5 out of 4.0, plus a GRE General score of at least 150 in the quantitative section (taken at a test centre, Home Edition not accepted, all three sections attempted). Direct PhD applicants must study full-time.

English: TOEFL iBT 91 (taken at a test centre, the Home Edition is not accepted) or academic IELTS overall 6.5, or equivalent. The FAQ says the test must have been taken within the 24 months before applying. The test requirement may be waived, subject to review and approval, for native English speakers from countries such as the US, UK, Canada, Australia and New Zealand, and for graduates of English-medium institutions who show IELTS 6.0 or TOEFL iBT 79 (or equivalent) at admission to their completed degree. Even then, English proof must be uploaded.

Also required: two referee recommendations, a statement of purpose, a research statement for PhD, and an admission interview. Degrees must come from an institution accredited and approved by the UAE Ministry of Education; applicants with degrees from outside the UAE need the Ministry's recognition (equivalency) certificate. Research Path and Study Path eligibility is reassessed every year. Separate awards for UAE citizens (Combined Master-PhD) and Chinese citizens (CSC-KU Joint PhD) exist and are not part of this scholarship.
age_experience_notes: No age limit or work-experience requirement is stated on the pages read.
funding_summary: Benefits depend on the tier. Master's Tiers I and II give full tuition, textbooks, free accommodation for eligible full-time students, medical insurance, mobilization and demobilization flights and UAE visa fees; Tier III gives a 50% tuition waiver and the non-tuition support except accommodation; Tier IV gives no tuition waiver but still textbooks, insurance, flights and visa fees. PhD Research Path Tiers I to III pay a basic stipend of AED 20,000 per month, with an extra monthly allowance in Tiers I and II; Study Path Tier I pays AED 4,000 and Tier II AED 2,000 per month. Tuition waivers for PhD run from full down to 25% depending on tier. Eligibility is reassessed each year. The pages do not state a total number of years of funding.
programmes_note: Master's and PhD programmes across the College of Engineering and Physical Sciences, the College of Computing and Mathematical Sciences and the College of Medicine and Health Sciences. The scholarship page itself names no programmes; the lists below come from the university's programme page. Fall 2027 PhD applications are open; the page says Master's applicants can register interest to be told when Master's applications open. Direct PhD applicants and Master's Tiers I-II must study full-time; PhD Study Path Tiers III and IV may study part-time.
institutions_note: The scholarship is held only at Khalifa University of Science and Technology in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates.

summary.detail: Scholarship tiers I to IV, mapped at admission. Tier I and II: full tuition, textbooks, free accommodation (eligible full-time students), medical insurance, flights and UAE visa fees. Tier III: 50% tuition waiver with textbooks, insurance, flights and visa fees. Tier IV: no tuition waiver, but textbooks, insurance, flights and visa fees. No monthly stipend is listed for Master's students; the FAQ says they may earn pay for services such as teaching, which is not mandatory. Normal completion time for full-time students is one academic year (FAQ). Entry: bachelor's CGPA 3.0/4.0.

summary.detail: Two paths. Research Path (full-time only, work commitment): Tier I full tuition with AED 20,000 basic monthly stipend plus an extra AED 20,000 allowance; Tier II full tuition, AED 20,000 stipend plus extra AED 10,000; Tier III 75% tuition waiver and AED 20,000 stipend; Tier IV 50% tuition waiver and free accommodation. Study Path (no work commitment): Tier I full tuition and AED 4,000 monthly stipend; Tier II 75% waiver and AED 2,000 stipend; Tier III 50% waiver; Tier IV 25% waiver; Tiers III and IV may be full- or part-time. Other support listed in tiers: textbooks, medical insurance, flights, UAE visa fees, conference support (subject to approval, Tiers I-II and Research Path Tier III). Entry: see eligibility (regular PhD or direct PhD).

benefits.limit_text: Master's: full waiver in Tiers I and II, 50% in Tier III, none in Tier IV. PhD Research Path: full in Tiers I and II, 75% in Tier III, 50% in Tier IV. PhD Study Path: full in Tier I, 75% in Tier II, 50% in Tier III, 25% in Tier IV.
benefits.conditions: The tier is set during admission and stated in the offer; eligibility is reassessed each year for PhD. Tuition rates (per FAQ): Master's AED 5,000 per credit hour, doctorate AED 6,666 per credit hour.

benefits.limit_text: PhD Research Path: AED 20,000 per month basic stipend (Tiers I-III) plus an additional monthly allowance of AED 20,000 (Tier I) or AED 10,000 (Tier II). PhD Study Path: AED 4,000 per month (Tier I) or AED 2,000 per month (Tier II). No stipend for Master's.
benefits.conditions: The additional allowance is subject to approval and progression criteria, which the page does not describe. Residence rent per semester is deducted from the monthly stipend (graduate FAQ). Study Path Tiers III-IV and Research Path Tier IV list no stipend.

benefits.limit_text: Free university accommodation for eligible full-time students
benefits.conditions: Master's Tiers I and II; PhD Research Path Tier IV; PhD Study Path all four tiers. Not listed for Master's Tiers III-IV or PhD Research Path Tiers I-III.

benefits.limit_text: Medical insurance for full-time international students sponsored by the university
benefits.conditions: Listed in every Master's and PhD tier.
For full-time overseas international students; listed in every Master's and PhD tier.

benefits.limit_text: UAE visa application fees covered; textbooks provided by the university

requirements.text: Application fee of AED 200, VAT included, paid when the application is submitted.
Certified copy of the bachelor's or master's degree certificate.

Equivalency (recognition) certificate from the UAE Ministry of Education for degrees from outside the UAE. The page says this is a lengthy process, so start early; the university is not involved in it.
requirements.conditional_rule: Degrees from institutions outside the UAE

requirements.text: Official transcript showing the grading scale (a grading scale is mandatory).
English score certificate (IELTS, TOEFL or EmSAT). TOEFL reports can be sent by the testing institution to the university using TOEFL code 0960. Must be uploaded even if an exemption applies.
GRE General score report, quantitative score at least 150; official reports sent with GRE code 0822.
Statement of purpose, 500 to 1,000 words, covering your interests and motivation, why this programme, what you hope to gain, career aims and how earlier study and work relate.

Research statement, 500 to 1,000 words: research interests and goals, experience so far, and an example project you would like to join. Applicants are told to read the university's research priorities first.
Two recommendations from people who know your academic work, sent through an online reference form. Referees get an automatic email after you submit; hard-copy or emailed letters are not accepted.
Passport-style photograph on a white background (JPEG, up to 2 MB).
Copy of valid passport. International applicants living in the UAE must also upload a valid UAE visa copy.

requirements.conditional_rule: Applicants living in the UAE (nationals and internationals)

requirements.text: File format: the FAQ says uploaded documents must be PDF up to 4 MB each (the requirements page also lists Word or scanned image files). Documents must be scanned clearly and legibly. Submitted documents become university property and are not returned.

application_steps.title: Choose a programme and check admission requirements
application_steps.detail: Pick one Master's or PhD programme from the university's list and read the admission requirements and the postgraduate scholarship pages. Applicants may apply to only one programme per semester. For Fall 2027 the admissions page says PhD applications are open and close on 1 February 2027; Master's applicants can register interest to be told when Master's applications open.

application_steps.title: Submit the online application and pay the AED 200 fee
application_steps.detail: Apply through the university's postgraduate application system. After submitting you land on a status page where you upload all documents. There is no separate scholarship form; the scholarships overview page says to indicate interest in scholarship support on the admission application. Submitted applications cannot be edited; changes are requested by email to the admissions office.

application_steps.title: Upload documents and make sure referees reply
application_steps.detail: Upload the certified degree certificate, transcript with grading scale, English score, CV, statements, photo and passport copy, plus GRE for direct PhD. Two referees complete an online form; the application is incomplete without these and incomplete applications are not considered. Applicants finishing their degree after the deadline can apply with transcripts to date and a letter confirming expected graduation.

application_steps.title: Admission review, interview and tier mapping
application_steps.detail: Shortlisted applicants are normally invited to an interview before a final decision. Scholarship eligibility is assessed during admission: applicants are mapped to tier I to IV using academic merit, research potential (PhD) and other factors. Places are limited and meeting the minimum criteria does not guarantee an award.

application_steps.title: Decision and scholarship tier in the admission offer
application_steps.detail: Admitted applicants are normally told by email no later than eight weeks after the application deadline; the university cannot give status updates on individual applications. Scholarships are subject to availability and confirmed at the end of the admission process, and the tier is stated in the admission offer. Rejected applicants may apply for the next semester.

application_steps.title: Submit official documents before registering for classes
application_steps.detail: Accepted applicants must hand in all official documents before registering for classes, or the class registration is cancelled. Applicants with degrees from outside the UAE must obtain the Ministry of Education recognition certificate and complete any attestation, notarisation or translation before travelling to the UAE.

application_steps.title: Keep the award: yearly reassessment and work commitment
application_steps.detail: PhD scholarship eligibility (Research Path and Study Path) is reassessed every year and the additional allowance depends on approval and progression criteria. Research Path students commit to work for Khalifa University or a nominated entity after graduation for a period equal to their period of study; the university may decline to offer a post for any reason. Full-time students may use university residences, with rent deducted from the monthly stipend.

The FAQ gives the Master's normal completion time as one academic year; some programmes may differ.
The stored summary said Study Path Tier II gives 75% waiver and AED 2,000: confirmed. Stored 'Master's Tier I and II include UAE visa fees' confirmed.
Admissions page lists EmSAT among accepted English tests in the document list and exemptions but not in the minimum-score list; the minimum scores stated are for TOEFL and IELTS only.
